issues.description: The template's Farm.java does not match the problem specification or the solution: the template declares a class named AnimalFarm (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java:3) and contains duplicated/malformed content (including an inner 'package' declaration inside a method and duplicated class skeleton). The problem statement and UML expect a class named Farm with specific attributes and methods (see problem_statement.md UML around lines 16-23 and 56-63). The solution implements a class named Farm with a private List<Animal> animals, constructor, getter/setter, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java). As-is the template will not compile and will confuse or block students (they will expect to implement/extend a Farm class matching the UML but the provided file has the wrong name and syntax errors).
issues.suggested_fix:
Replace the provided template file with a correct Farm skeleton that matches the problem UML and the solution. Specifically:
- Rename the class to 'Farm' (public class Farm) and ensure the file is package-declared only at the top (remove any inner 'package' statements).
- Provide the private attribute 'List<Animal> animals' and initialize it in a no-argument constructor (new ArrayList<>()).
- Include getter and setter for animals, addAnimal(Animal a), feedAllAnimals(), and the private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal) and public singFarmSong() stubs matching the signatures used in the problem/solution.
This will ensure the template compiles and students can implement the intended design without being blocked by wrong class names or syntax errors.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution describe and implement a class named 'Farm' (the core entity representing the farm and its animals). The template repository file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, however, declares a class named 'AnimalFarm' instead of 'Farm'. This naming mismatch breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description/tests (which expect a Farm class) and the starter code: students and automated tests will look for/attempt to use a class named Farm (e.g., Main and tests call new Farm()), but the template provides AnimalFarm, causing compilation/test failures and unnecessary confusion about which class to implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the class in the template to match the problem statement and solution: change the declaration 'public class AnimalFarm' to 'public class Farm' in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java (and ensure the class name matches the file name). Also remove or correct the stray duplicate package/declaration lines inside the file so the template provides a clean Farm class skeleton that students and tests can directly use.
